disclaimer: These are simulated-persona reviews generated by AI agents, not interviews with real coaches. They supplement rather than replace human feedback.
expectations: I expect one place to cut game film, check the frames behind a label and pass reviewed snaps on to scouting and our weekly plan.
This is for the invited coaches on one football staff. I would own the line work and my coordinator would sign off on the unit plan.
Ten minutes in I expect to have a cut open, check its boundaries and correct one visible label or leave it unknown.

tasks.title: Sign in, find the game and open work
tasks.attempted: Selected the listed OL demo identity, signed in, read the dashboard and opened Schedule.
tasks.observed: The account picker filled the demo password. This position-coach account went directly to the workspace. Staff and Settings showed MFA Off. The dashboard and schedule agreed on Week 10 at Westmoor, Fri, Oct 30 at 7:00 PM. The dashboard listed 16 cuts, a rejected upload and a failed inference job. No fixture was added.
tasks.note: I can find my game and see the cuts waiting before I open film.

tasks.title: Find the newest upload and interpret a proposed cut
tasks.attempted: Followed the dashboard cut count, opened film, compared the three upload dates, opened the Oct 25 file and then the Oct 21 ready file.
tasks.observed: The cut count opened Opponent Scouting. The newest seeded asset, westmoor_vs_caldwell_endzone.mp4, showed Segment at 38%, a thumbnail retry and “No plays proposed yet.” It still had no cuts when reopened later. In the older ready film I could read proposed Play 32 at 68:23–68:30, a 7.4-second auto cut in the review queue. I could not explain a cut from the requested newest asset.
tasks.note: I can read the start and end on the older game. On the newer game all I can tell my coordinator is that processing is still running.

tasks.title: Check the evidence behind a proposed label
tasks.attempted: Opened Formation for play 5, followed its 10:35–10:38 evidence interval and selected the 638.1-second provenance frame.
tasks.observed: The panel called i_form a confident, unreviewed model proposal. The browser video landed at the end of its 6.34-second mock clip. The selected timeline row stayed on play 32. On a repeat the page displayed the requested playhead of 10:38 while the video control was already at its end. The label could be traced to a stated source time, but its frame could not be inspected in this mock.
tasks.note: I would count the backs before I let that formation onto our sheet. A timestamp by itself doesn’t show me who is in the backfield.

tasks.title: Find permitted and restricted staff actions
tasks.attempted: Visited Playbook, Personnel, Staff and the offense plan after checking Schedule in G1. Wrote and posted a comment on the offense draft.
tasks.observed: The comment appeared in the plan. Staff identified the OL membership as position coach, Offense, and said only the head coach manages membership. The role could also inspect the roster, packages and playbook concepts. The observed differences fit the contract.
tasks.note: I can leave the guard’s first-step question for the coordinator and let the head coach handle invitations.

tasks.title: Try to approve and change retention
tasks.attempted: Opened the defense tab on Plans, inspected the eligible in-review version and tried the retention field on Settings.
tasks.observed: Defense v1 was in review with read/comment guidance and no Approve control. The 365-day retention input was disabled, and clicking it left it unchanged. The page said “Only the head coach can change retention.” Neither path submitted a forbidden operation.
tasks.note: Film retention is the head coach’s call. That sentence tells me who can change it.

tasks.title: Upload film and work through the keyboard queue
tasks.attempted: Uploaded a six-second synthetic MP4 as offense/end zone, followed its processing jobs, clicked a thumbnail and used the README’s listbox shortcut guidance to try N, accept and reject. Also tested consecutive keys in the seeded queue.
tasks.observed: The mock estimated the upload at 30 seconds, completed its jobs and proposed three cuts. The still-open timeline showed 0 queued and N selected nothing. I manually accepted cut 2 and rejected cut 3. Revisiting put the remaining proposal in the queue. On the seeded asset N selected cut 33, A accepted it and selected 34, but keyboard focus left the list. The following N left 34 selected.
tasks.note: I want one hand on the keyboard for the fourth quarter. The cuts are on screen. Why am I hunting for the queue again?

tasks.title: Split a segment and merge its pieces
tasks.attempted: Played the first cut on disposable line-practice.mp4, tried to split near the start, moved to an interior point, split and merged the two resulting pieces.
tasks.observed: A near-start split showed a move-the-playhead message. At approximately 0:06, the 0:02–0:09 cut became 4.3- and 2.7-second pieces. The count rose from three to four. Merge with next restored one 7.0-second Coach merged cut, with three total. Both split pieces and the merged result displayed Proposed, not queued.
tasks.note: I can get the original seven seconds back, and I can see that it was my merge. I would want the next review pass to pick the revised cut up.

tasks.title: Accept, correct, mark unknown and reject labels
tasks.attempted: In the ready seed I corrected play 5 Formation, reopened its history, accepted play 5 Unit, left play 6 Personnel unknown and rejected play 6 Motion with a reason. All edits were disposable workflow tests.
tasks.observed: History showed i_form → two-back set, my reason, reviewer and time. The panel also listed the model, prompt and six frame times. The football terminology could be entered as free text. The grid showed the accepted unit, unknown personnel and rejected motion. The corrected value still displayed the model’s word “confident” in its cell.
tasks.note: I can write “two-back set” in our language and see what I changed. I would open the history before treating that confidence word as a judgment on my correction.

tasks.title: Read, cancel and confirm bulk acceptance
tasks.attempted: Filtered to Hash, counted 48 rows, opened the dialog, canceled and compared the rows. Reopened, confirmed the five eligible values, checked an excluded play-type cell and inspected an untouched Hash.
tasks.observed: Cancel preserved the rows. Confirmation changed five Hash labels, left two inferred abstentions alone and left play 7 Play type untouched. The dialog called 41 labels “already reviewed,” including untouched Hash values for plays 13–48. Play 13 explicitly said “not reviewed.” After saving, the key filter reset to All keys with 42 eligible values.
tasks.note: I’m willing to confirm five hashes. I need to know how much film nobody has graded yet before I tell the coordinator we’re done.

tasks.title: Enter the prototype through research first
tasks.attempted: Opened /prototype/#/research in a fresh context, checked the blank time estimate, chose “I’m not sure,” the spreadsheet method and Yes for prior exposure, then followed the team brief and demo film to the queue.
tasks.observed: No numeric baseline was entered. The research entry asked about exposure before displaying candidate grades. The queue forecast four gradable snaps out of six and named plays 3 and 6 as likely abstentions. I used another clean context for the demo.
tasks.note: I don’t have a defensible stopwatch number for six snaps. I’m glad I can say so without putting in a guess.

tasks.title: Assess confidence, decide blind and interpret No Grade
tasks.attempted: In /prototype/#/demo followed play 2’s contact evidence, saved play 3’s abstention with “Cannot confirm it is No. 62,” then inspected play 4’s contact and result frames before submitting a blind grade.
tasks.observed: Play 2 distinguished High identity confidence from Medium grade confidence; its 00:13.1 link selected Contact. Play 3 described an obscured identity and off-camera contact. On play 4 I chose No Grade first. The revealed Grade 1 had High confidence and acknowledged uncertainty about the guard’s assignment. I kept No Grade with “Assignment unclear.” Neither High nor No Grade was misread during this run.
tasks.note: A defender gets through, but I can’t pin that gap on the guard from this angle. I’m keeping my first call.

tasks.title: Edit a practice focus, revise evidence and export
tasks.attempted: Finished six decisions, traced the hand-placement focus to plays 2 and 5, edited it, then revised play 5 with a reason and returned. Accepted the rebuilt focus, completed feedback and downloaded the session JSON.
tasks.observed: The edited cue appeared with 3 coach-graded plays of 6 reviewed. Plays 3, 4 and 6 were explicitly excluded as No Grade. The saved change to play 5 left one supporting play and triggered “Stale — review again.” The demo export had mode demo and baseline null. The timing table said the exploratory comparison was not computed.
tasks.note: If I change one of the two examples, make me look at the coaching point again. A single play gives me a clip to teach from, not a weekly trend.

interview.answer: I could find my cuts and leave a useful grading record, but following a frame link took me to the end of the demo clip.

The landing page promised cuts and labels with evidence attached. I found the timestamps, the original formation and the place to correct it. I expected to be looking at that exact snap when I clicked 638.1 seconds.

Saturday night I do boundaries and first-pass grades; Sunday I check anything I owe the coordinator. The reason and history fit that handoff. Reacquiring keyboard focus after accepting cut 33 fights the way I work down a list.

I had three new cuts in front of me and “Next in queue (0).” After I left and returned the remaining proposal showed up. I also had to open a Hash row to work out why the bulk dialog counted it as reviewed.

I trusted the record of my formation change because I could reopen it and see both values and my reason. On play 4 I kept No Grade even after the High-confidence Grade 1 appeared. The frame showed penetration, but it didn’t settle whose job that defender was.
I would stop signing off on labels if the only evidence I could reach was a different play. I’ll still flag the cut for someone who can open the original.
First, have the evidence link select the right play and show a frame I can check. Second, tell me which of the skipped labels nobody has reviewed before I accept anything in bulk.
Keep the blind-first grade, the words explaining what would make a snap gradable and the warning when a changed grade makes the practice focus stale. Those are decisions I need to make myself.

Conditional for my own use and for a staff recommendation. I would pilot it alongside my sheet once the cited snap is reachable. I would recommend it to the staff when the queue works from the keyboard and the bulk counts distinguish untouched labels.
The focus named plays 2 and 5 and told me exactly which three snaps it left out. I could bring those two plays to a meeting. I can’t use this exercise to claim any number of hours saved.

findings.title: A label’s frame link cannot show the cited snap in the mock player
findings.element: Formation, play 5 · evidence and provenance timestamps
findings.observed: Clicking 638.1s for play 5 ended at the 6.34-second mock clip boundary while play 32 stayed selected. Repeating the jump showed 10:38 in the page readout beside the ended player and the 68:23–68:30 timeline selection. The page identifies its proxy as a short stand-in.
findings.expected: A frame link should select its source play and either show matching evidence or explain that the specific frame is unavailable.
findings.proposed_change: Select the source cut and display a matching demo frame or an explicit unavailable-frame state at the requested timestamp.
findings.quote: I can read the label, but I can’t sign my name to that formation from the picture I was given.

findings.title: Bulk acceptance counts untouched labels as already reviewed
findings.observed: The confirmation counted 5 eligible Hash labels, 2 abstentions and 41 “already reviewed.” Hash on plays 13–48 had no model output. Reopening play 13 explicitly showed “not reviewed.” Cancel kept the data unchanged and confirm accepted only the five eligible values.
findings.expected: The count of reviewed work should include only labels a coach reviewed so the remaining grading workload is visible.
findings.proposed_change: Report untouched unknowns, abstentions and previously reviewed labels as separate counts in the confirmation.
findings.quote: If you tell me 41 were reviewed, I’m going to think somebody did that work.

findings.title: Cuts produced while an upload is open miss the keyboard queue
findings.element: Segment job completion · Plays and Next in queue
findings.observed: After the mock segment job completed, all three generated cuts were marked Proposed and “not queued.” Next in queue showed zero and N selected nothing. Manual decisions worked. Leaving and reopening the asset put the remaining untouched proposal in the queue. New split and merged proposals were also shown outside the queue.
findings.expected: A coach who stays on the asset to watch processing should be able to start reviewing the new proposals immediately.
findings.proposed_change: Add newly produced proposals to the live queue when segmentation, split or merge refreshes the list.
findings.quote: I stayed on the upload waiting for the cuts. I shouldn’t have to leave it to start grading.

findings.title: Accepting a cut drops keyboard focus from the queue
findings.element: Plays listbox · A followed by N
findings.observed: With focus in the list, N selected cut 33 and A accepted it and selected cut 34. The active DOM element changed from the listbox to the page body. A subsequent physical N left cut 34 selected. Targeting the list again was necessary for more keyboard commands.
findings.expected: The next selected cut should receive keyboard input as soon as the previous decision is saved.
findings.proposed_change: Restore keyboard focus to the timeline listbox after saving a cut and selecting the next proposal.
findings.quote: The highlight moved to the next snap, so I thought my keys were still there.

findings.title: The dashboard cut-review task opens Opponent Scouting
findings.element: Open tasks · “16 proposed play cuts are waiting for review.”
findings.observed: Selecting the 16-cut task opened the Opponent Scouting findings for Westmoor. I navigated separately to Our Team Film and the ready asset to reach its timeline.
findings.expected: A cut-review work item should open the film and the first pending cut.
findings.proposed_change: Link the task to the ready asset’s pending segment queue.
findings.quote: I clicked a job about cuts and landed on formation tendencies.

findings.title: Bulk acceptance resets the key filter and expands the next action
findings.observed: After confirmation, the active filter changed from Hash to All keys. The view grew from 48 labels to 384 and the next bulk button offered 42 eligible values. A fresh selection of Hash showed zero eligible values. No unintended values changed in this run.
findings.expected: The review scope should persist after a successful batch action, with a visible result for that batch.
findings.proposed_change: Preserve the active filters and show the completed batch counts after refreshing the grid.
findings.quote: I’m still working on hashes. Why is the next button offering me 42 other decisions?

findings.title: The corrected value displays confidence from the original proposal
findings.element: Play 5 Formation cell after a correction
findings.observed: I changed the model’s i_form to two-back set. The resulting grid cell read “two-back set” and “confident,” and its accessible name included “Corrected, confident.” The side panel distinguished the confident model proposal from the separate coach correction.
findings.expected: A quick scan should make clear whose value the confidence word describes.
findings.proposed_change: Label the confidence as belonging to the original model proposal when displaying a coach-corrected value.
findings.quote: That was my edit. Seeing “confident” underneath makes me open the history to check who said it.

findings.title: The newest seeded film has no cut available for the first walkthrough
findings.element: Caldwell upload · processing jobs and proposed plays
findings.observed: The newest seeded Week 10 upload showed a segment job at 38%, a thumbnail retry and no proposed plays at first open and again at a later recheck. Reviewing a cut required switching to the older ready Stonebrook film. The screen explained the running job.
findings.expected: A first-time reviewer should be able to find a playable example from the processing state.
findings.proposed_change: Offer a link to the latest ready game film beside the empty-cut state while processing continues.
findings.quote: I can see why there’s nothing to grade yet. Give me a way to get to film I can work on now.

keep: The correction panel keeps the original proposal, current coach value, free-text reason, reviewer and frame provenance together.
The prototype withholds the play 4 candidate until the coach submits an independent grade.
Play 3 explains the missing evidence and asks for a reason before saving No Grade.
The practice focus names supporting and excluded plays, and a saved revision marks the focus stale.
The Hash bulk confirmation can be canceled without changing rows, and confirmation skipped the two inferred abstentions tested.

verdict.condition: I would pilot it alongside my spreadsheet once evidence links reach the cited snap. I would recommend it to the staff once the keyboard queue survives a save and the bulk dialog counts untouched labels correctly.
